title: The Shiva Sutras, with the Varttika
author: vasugupta
attributionNote: The tradition holds that Vasugupta received these sutras in a dream and found them inscribed on a rock at the foot of a tree; they were written down in the ninth century. The Varttika read beside them is the commentary of the tenth-century Kashmiri tradition.
description: In seventy-two aphorisms the Shiva Sutras teach that consciousness is the one reality and that its freedom is the power of acting: the bound soul is that same consciousness contracted, gnawing at the food of its own ignorance. The path is given as practice, knowledge and will, and the reader is told that the self is the actor and the act, and that entering the highest state is a matter of recognition rather than attainment.
historicalContext: The base text of Kashmirian Shaivism, and the short scripture that Kshemaraja, Abhinavagupta's disciple, expanded into the commentary the school's practice rests on. The Tantraloka of Abhinavagupta, held elsewhere in this library, is its long philosophical development.
availabilityNote: Complete: all three sections of the sutras (75 units) from the GRETIL e-text, each sutra streamed at read time, with the Varttika commentary in a second pane. The commentary repeats each sutra's reference with several units of its own, so its pane carries more lines than the root text.
